reconstruction.text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. For every real polynomial p, there exists a family h of square-integrability witnesses, one for every w in E, such that f_w(x)=p(<w,x>) is gamma_E-almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite squared integral, and the map F_p:E -> L^2(gamma_E; R), F_p(w)=[f_w], formed using h(w), is infinitely continuously Frechet differentiable over R on all of E. The family h is quantified after E and p and covers every w; smoothness is in the L^2 norm with respect to w.
